A Big Problem in the Bitcoin Futures Market: A Few Large Traders Hold Most of the Positions—If Something Goes Wrong, Who Will Be the Buyer?

Research warns that BTC futures open interest is excessively concentrated. In extreme market conditions, this could trigger a chain of destabilization and hit the entire market.

The latest research cited by Crypto Briefing shows that trader concentration in the Bitcoin futures market is too high—simply put, most open contracts are held by just a few large traders. When the market is calm, it’s fine. But if a black-swan event occurs and these big players simultaneously cut positions or get liquidated, liquidity can vanish in an instant. Prices could then fall at a speed far beyond expectations, and the shock may even spill over into traditional financial markets.

BTC is currently at $63,507.09, up 0.70% over the past 24 hours. The market hasn’t priced in this structural risk yet.

One-sentence translation: The “foundation” of the futures market is thinner than it looks—the positioning moves of a handful of whales can shake the entire room.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Neutral. This is not a sudden negative catalyst; it’s a structural risk warning. The price likely won’t plunge just because of a research report. BTC will most likely continue to trade in a range around $63,507.
- Medium term: Regulators may use this as a basis to increase scrutiny of concentration in futures positions. Exchanges could be required to disclose more large-trader position data. High-leverage players should recognize that in extreme conditions, slippage will far exceed what they imagine.

My take
This is information that falls under “we know it, but it doesn’t change how we act for now.” In the short term, the bias is neutral-to-stable. Support for BTC is around $75.44K, while resistance is also at $75.44K. The real risk will only materialize if an event is triggered (a black swan, or an exchange incident). For spot holders, this is actually a warning: in a market where futures positions are concentrated, liquidation can happen faster than stopping-out orders.

- Asset: BTC
- Direction: Neutral; no clear upside or downside driver within 12 hours
- Duration: 12 hours

It’s not about how much it’s up—it’s about the fact that its volume and momentum are more solid than those altcoins that are basically just flash-in-the-pan. Truth is, in times like this when things grind and churn, people are prone to make two mistakes. One is complaining the market is too slow, so they open their full positions waiting for a breakout. I genuinely feel that during a consolidation phase, what’s most valuable isn’t who guesses the direction correctly—it’s who has thicker “hands,” meaning more ammo. Honestly, seeing today’s market action was my first instinct to rub my eyes.

PORTAL surged 57% in a day, GPS rose 37%, and BTW even jumped 26%—but what about BTC? Against the king of coins, these altcoins are like playing a whole different-dimension game. BTC only moved 0.7% in 24 hours, and over 7 days it’s still negative. The price is stuck at 63,469—neither up nor down—just like a hesitant retail trader standing at a crossroads.

Look at it another way—this kind of market is exactly the most interesting time.

Let’s start with BTC. 63,469—this number gives me a slightly uneasy feeling. The Fear & Greed Index is sitting right at 50, neutral—not cold, not hot—like a cup of water left sitting too long. The funding rate is 0.0089%, perfectly normal. So what does it mean? It means the market isn’t in extreme fear, nor is it in狂热 greed. Everyone is watching, waiting for a directional signal.

Personally, I don’t think this is a bad thing. BTC is consolidating around the 63k level, and in reality it’s digesting the earlier gains and selling pressure. A 7-day pullback of -2.3%—honestly, that’s pretty mild for the middle of a bull market. I think the key in the next few days is whether it can hold above 63k. If it can break 65k with volume, then this consolidation is basically over. If it falls below 62k, it may have to grind for a while longer.

But what’s worth discussing today isn’t BTC—it’s this monster called PORTAL.

+57.92%, 320M USDT in 24-hour trading volume. For a token priced at 0.0175 dollars, that volume is already pretty outrageous. I checked its intro—"Onboarding the first billion gamers into Web3". Bringing the first billion game players into Web3. Wow—this narrative, in 2026, honestly feels a bit retro. The GameFi concept was hyped in 2021 for a round, and now it’s being brought up again. And the market actually buys it?

This makes me think of a classic question: are we炒故事, or are we炒筹码结构? A price of 0.0175 dollars means it’s already down more than 90% from the high. This kind of rebound is more likely an oversold bounce plus short-term speculative trading by smart money, not a fundamental turnaround. Funding rate is 0.1104%—wait, that number is for BTW, not PORTAL. But BTW’s funding rate is definitely worth noting: 0.1104% puts it in the long “overheated” zone. A 26% jump paired with overheated funding rates is usually not a good sign.

My logic is simple: chasing this kind of heat doesn’t make the risk-reward ratio worth it. If you’re already on the train, set a trailing stop to protect your profits. If you’re not on board yet, I suggest staying calm and waiting for a pullback. At 0.0175 dollars, there’s a dense trapped-supply area overhead, so selling pressure won’t be light.

In contrast, GPS’s +37.62% is actually more interesting. GoPlus focuses on Web3 user security—this sector has real demand in 2026. But with a price of 0.0148 dollars and 82M in成交額, honestly it’s still in the category of small-cap bet games. I usually just observe coins like this and don’t jump in lightly.

Next, let’s talk about the biggest losers. H is -27.69%, XPIN -19.45%, ACU is -18.75%—I don’t really have much to say about these. If they fell this much, either the project screwed up somehow, or they were pumped too hard earlier and now they’re paying the debt. ACU’s funding rate still shows normal, but the price has already dropped nearly 20%—that kind of divergence is worth being cautious about.

On the hot search list, Pudgy Penguins and Hyperliquid are still there. That’s kind of interesting. PENGU, as a representative of turning NFTs into meme coins, can keep occupying the hot searches—suggesting the market still has enthusiasm for this kind of asset. But high heat doesn’t necessarily mean money is being made. And I think many people get this mixed up.

Back to BTC and ETH. ETH is slightly stronger than BTC today: +1.00%, and the price is at 1,898. It’s just one step away from the 2,000 psychological level. I think if ETH can hold above 1,920 in the next few days, the odds of pushing toward 2,000 will increase a lot. After all, in 2026 ETH’s narrative is richer than BTC’s—staking, Layer2, RWA—these are all real, tangible application scenarios.

My trading plan is like this: for BTC, in the 62,500–63,000 range you can consider building a position in batches to bet on the upward direction. Put the stop-loss at 61,800. First target is 65,000. If it breaks through, then look toward 67,000. For ETH, you can test a position around 1,880, with a stop-loss at 1,840, and a target of 1,980–2,000. Of course, this is only my thinking. The market always has different voices—everyone should still make decisions based on their own risk tolerance.

Finally, what I want to say is: today’s kind of market—BTC is chopping sideways, while altcoins fly all over the place—is actually when it tests people the most. Seeing PORTAL double in a day—are you itchy inside? Seeing the red losses on the losers list—are you panicking? These are all normal emotional reactions, but the people who truly make money are often those who can stay calm amid the noise.

Today’s PORTAL and BTW—who’s it going to be tomorrow? The market never lacks opportunities; what it lacks is patience and discipline. Do you think PORTAL’s rebound can keep going, or is it just a one-off bloom? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.

但今天真正值得聊的不是BTC，是PORTAL这个怪物。

+57.92%，24小时成交3.2亿USDT，对于一个0.0175美元的代币来说，这个交易量已经相当夸张了。我翻了翻它的简介——"Onboarding the first billion gamers into Web3"，把第一个十亿游戏玩家带入Web3。好家伙，这个叙事放在2026年，说实话有点复古了。GameFi这个概念在2021年就炒过一轮，现在又拿出来翻炒，市场居然还买账？

这让我想到一个很经典的问题：到底是在炒叙事，还是在炒筹码结构？0.0175美元的价格，意味着它从高点已经跌去了90%以上。这种级别的反弹，更多可能是超跌反弹加上游资短炒，而不是什么基本面反转。资金费率0.1104%——等等，这个数字是BTW的，不是PORTAL的。但BTW这个资金费率确实值得注意，0.1104%已经属于多头过热区间了。26%的涨幅配上过热的资金费率，这通常不是什么好信号。

我的思路很简单：这种热度追进去，风险收益比不划算。如果你已经在车上，可以设个移动止损保护利润；如果还没上车，我建议冷静一下，等回调再说。0.0175美元这个位置，上方套牢盘密集，抛压不会小。

相比之下，GPS的+37.62%倒是有点意思。GoPlus做的是Web3用户安全，这个赛道在2026年其实是有真实需求的。但0.0148美元的价格和82M的成交额，说实话还是属于小市值博弈的范畴。这种币我一般只做观察，不轻易参与。

再说说跌幅榜。H -27.69%，XPIN -19.45%，ACU -18.75%——这几个币我都没什么好说的，跌成这样要么是项目方出了幺蛾子，要么就是前期炒太猛了在还债。ACU的资金费率还显示正常，但价格已经跌了快20%，这种背离现象值得警惕。

热搜榜上Pudgy Penguins和Hyperliquid还在，这倒是挺有意思的。PENGU作为NFT转meme币的代表，能持续占据热搜，说明市场对这类资产还是有热情的。但热度高不代表能赚钱，这一点我觉得很多人都搞混了。

说回BTC和ETH。ETH今天表现比BTC稍微强一点，+1.00%，价格来到1,898。距离2,000的心理关口就差一步之遥了。我觉得ETH如果能在接下来几天站上1,920，那冲2,000的概率会大大增加。毕竟ETH的叙事在2026年其实比BTC更丰富——质押、Layer2、RWA，这些都是实打实的应用场景。

我的交易思路是这样的：BTC在62,500-63,000区间可以考虑分批建仓看多方向，止损放在61,800，第一目标65,000，如果突破就看向67,000。ETH的话，1,880附近可以试探性布局，止损1,840，目标1,980-2,000。当然这只是我的思路，市场总有不同声音，大家还是要根据自己的风险承受能力来做判断。

最后我想说的是，今天这种行情——大饼横盘、山寨乱飞——其实是最考验人的时候。看着PORTAL一天翻倍，你心里痒不痒？看着跌幅榜上的血亏，你慌不慌？这些都是正常的情绪反应，但真正赚钱的人，往往是那些能在热闹中保持冷静的人。

今天的PORTAL和BTW，明天的谁？市场永远不缺机会，缺的是耐心和纪律。你觉得PORTAL这波反弹还能持续吗？还是说只是昙花一现？欢迎在评论区聊聊你的看法。

Back when the market opened in the afternoon, $ETH  hovered around 1,900 for a long time, and the volume was 203 million.

It looks red, but in the past 24 hours it was still up 1.05%.

I used to die by this illusion.

I thought a high win rate means profit. In reality, every time I made 5%, I’d run—then when I lost, I kept holding all the way down to 20%.

My account equity curve was like a waterfall, but the win rate looked good.

Later I finally understood: take-profit needs to be held, and stop-loss needs to be cut hard.

The risk-reward ratio—that’s the real number that decides life or death.

Today’s market is the same too. A 1.05% gain and 203 million in volume—how many people can that really feed?

A high-win-rate style is to repeatedly take profit and cut losses at this level, and in the end it all gets fed to the trading fees.

I won’t bet on that little probability during low-volume conditions.

#BTC #ETH #投资哲学 #交易心态 #crypto

Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon kill 11, say they hit Hezbollah’s elite Radwan unit and killed a commander

Tensions in the Middle East’s regional flashpoints have flared again. According to multiple publicly available reports, the Israeli military recently carried out airstrikes in southern Lebanon. The Lebanese authorities reported at least 11 deaths, including children. Israel, meanwhile, claimed its strikes targeted related assets of Hezbollah’s elite Radwan forces and killed the commander, Hajj Hassan. The attack was described as the deadliest round of casualties since both sides reached a de-escalation framework agreement around June, and it quickly drove markets to reprice geopolitical risk.

In terms of the backdrop, after a period of high-intensity confrontation between Israel and Hezbollah, both sides around June had arranged to ease the tempo on the front lines under frameworks such as “toward lasting peace.” Lebanese security forces gradually assumed control and reduced the presence of non-state armed groups, which became a key direction in the negotiation narrative. However, a ceasefire or de-escalation does not mean underlying structural contradictions disappear. Israel’s stated rationale for this operation is that Hezbollah launched attacks on what Israel calls the “security zone” in southern Lebanon, causing three Israeli personnel to be seriously injured, prompting Israel to carry out a counterstrike. Lebanon, on the other hand, emphasized that the airstrikes caused civilian casualties, including women and children, underscoring that the ceasefire has not broken the cycle of “low-intensity friction—high-intensity retaliation.”

The core facts can be summarized in three points. First, the strike locations were concentrated in southern Lebanon, and Lebanon confirmed that 11 people were killed, including three children; this was also the deadliest wave reported publicly in the post-agreement period. Second, Israel announced that its targets were of a military nature, such as the headquarters of the Radwan unit, and named Hajj Hassan as having been killed. That claim currently comes mainly from Israeli statements, and public information has limited details on identity verification beyond the one-sided account. Third, a spokesperson for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told the media that the airstrike “should help move negotiations forward” and make the other side take them more seriously, reiterating that Israel still supports the U.S.-brokered arrangement and hopes the Lebanese armed forces can play a greater role in excluding Hezbollah’s influence. In other words, Israel is trying to frame military strikes as a tool of negotiation pressure rather than a straightforward escalation.

Logically, “tactical strikes” and “strategic intent” need to be separated. If Israel’s narrative holds, targeting elite command nodes aims to raise the cost of the opponent’s breach and force the Lebanese Armed Forces and the international mediating parties to accelerate the clearing of armed presence in the south. If Lebanon and regional forces characterize the incident as an infringement on civilians and sovereignty, it could spur retaliation, mobilization, and the postponement of talks. The June agreement matters because it temporarily pushed the conflict back from “full-scale fighting” to a track of “limited friction plus diplomatic oversight.” And once there are double-digit deaths involving children, domestic political pressure rises rapidly, making compromise by either side harder. The spokesperson’s emphasis on “pushing for more serious talks and avoiding the opposite effect” also indicates Israel is aware of the risk that military actions could anger the other side and damage the atmosphere for negotiations.

For the crypto market, the direct fundamentals chain does not originate from any single commander’s personal identity, but from how risk appetite and macro volatility transmit. The path is roughly: geopolitical conflict heats up → volatility in energy and safe-haven assets increases → global risk assets see position cuts or higher demand for hedging → more liquid crypto assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum simultaneously reflect changes in risk premium. Historically, sudden conflicts in the Middle East often first hit oil price expectations and U.S. dollar liquidity expectations, and then map into crypto volatility and leverage deleveraging. If the market interprets the situation as “localized, controllable, and still returning to negotiations,” the shock may be relatively short-lived. If it interprets it as “the agreement failing with multi-line linkages,” safe-haven and risk-asset selling pressure may occur at the same time. It’s important to clarify that the above is an analysis of transmission mechanisms, not a prediction of short-term price moves. Crypto assets are often treated as high-beta risk assets, and in some phases they are also assigned a “macro hedge” narrative; these roles can switch under different liquidity conditions.

Editor’s observation: current information remains highly dependent on accounts from the parties to the conflict and retransmissions by news agencies. Figures on civilian casualties, whether targets are purely military, and how far the verification of a commander’s identity has progressed will all shape subsequent narratives. More worth tracking than the airstrike itself is whether U.S. mediation will be restarted, whether the Lebanese Armed Forces’ takeover timeline shows substantive progress, and whether friction in the southern “security zone” is becoming continuous. For market participants, such events should be observed through a “geopolitical tail risk—volatility—liquidity” framework, avoiding the direct linear equation of military announcements with the direction of asset prices. On the factual level, the disclosed casualty figures and each side’s statements are what matter. As for whether negotiations can become “more serious” because of the strikes, this is still—at present—only Israel’s unilateral expectation and awaits validation through subsequent diplomatic interactions.

content:
以军空袭黎南致11死 称击毙真主党指挥官

中东局部冲突再度升温。据多方公开报道，以色列军方近期对黎巴嫩南部实施空袭，黎巴嫩方面通报造成至少11人死亡，其中包含儿童；以方则宣称在行动中打击真主党精锐拉德万部队相关目标，并击毙指挥官哈吉哈山。此轮袭击被描述为双方自6月达成缓和敌对行动相关框架协议以来，伤亡最为严重的一次，因此迅速牵动市场对地缘风险的重新定价。

从事件背景看，以色列与真主党在经历高强度对抗后，曾在6月前后围绕“迈向持久和平”等框架安排缓和前线节奏，黎巴嫩安全力量逐步接管、削弱非国家武装存在，是相关谈判叙事中的关键方向。然而停火或降级并不等于结构性矛盾消失。以方此次给出的行动理由是：真主党对以方所称黎南部“安全区”发动攻击，导致3名以军人员重伤，因而实施反击。黎方则强调空袭造成平民伤亡，包括妇女与儿童，凸显停火后“低烈度摩擦—高烈度报复”循环仍未切断。

核心事实可归纳为三点。第一，空袭地点集中在黎巴嫩南部，并被黎方证实造成11人丧生，其中有3名孩童；这也是协议后阶段公开报道中最致命的一波。第二，以色列宣布打击对象指向拉德万部队总部一类军事目标，并点名指挥官哈吉哈山已被击毙；该说法目前主要来自以方通报，公开信息中对身份细节仍以单方表述为主。第三，以色列总理尼坦雅胡的发言人随后对媒体表示，空袭“应能推动谈判重启，让对方更加认真”，并重申以方仍支持由美国斡旋的安排，希望黎巴嫩武装部队能够在排除真主党势力方面发挥更大作用。换言之，以方试图把军事打击解释为谈判施压工具，而非单纯升级。

逻辑上需要把“战术打击”和“战略意图”分开看。若以方叙事成立，打击精锐指挥节点，目的是提高对手违约成本，并迫使黎政府军与国际斡旋方加快清空南部武装存在；若黎方与地区力量将事件定性为对平民与主权的侵害，则可能刺激报复、动员与谈判搁置。6月协议之所以重要，是因为它把冲突从“全面交火”暂时推回“有限摩擦+外交管控”轨道；而一旦出现双位数死亡且涉及儿童，国内政治压力会迅速上升，任何一方妥协都更难。发言人强调“推动更认真谈判、避免反效果”，本身也说明以方清楚军事行动存在激怒对方、破坏谈判气氛的风险。

对加密市场而言，直接基本面链路并不来自某一指挥官个人，而来自风险偏好与宏观波动的传导。路径大致是：地缘冲突升温→能源与避险资产波动加大→全球风险资产出现仓位收缩或对冲需求上升→比特币、以太坊等流动性较好的加密资产同步反映风险溢价。历史上，中东突发冲突往往先冲击原油预期与美元流动性预期，再映射到加密市场的波动率与杠杆去化；若市场解读为“局部、可控、仍回到谈判”，冲击可能偏短；若解读为“协议失效、多线联动”，则避险与风险资产抛压可能并行出现。需要明确的是，上述为传导机制分析，而非对短期涨跌的判断；加密资产既常被当作高贝塔风险资产，也在部分阶段被赋予“宏观对冲”叙事，两种角色会在不同流动性环境中切换。

编辑观察是：当前信息仍高度依赖冲突双方与通讯社转述，平民伤亡数字、目标是否纯军事、指挥官身份核验进度，都会影响后续叙事。更值得跟踪的不是单次空袭本身，而是美国斡旋是否重启、黎政府军接管节奏有无实质进展，以及南部“安全区”摩擦是否连续化。对市场参与者来说，应把此类事件放入“地缘尾部风险—波动率—流动性”框架中观察，避免把军事通告直接线性等同于资产价格方向。事实层面以已披露伤亡与双方表态为准；关于谈判能否因打击而“更认真”，目前仍属以方单方面预期，尚待后续外交互动验证。

This Fed meeting set the rate at 3.5%-3.75%, unchanged—matching market expectations. The real twist is Japan: officials there also signaled that more hikes could come. One side—the world’s largest central bank—presses the brakes, while Japan, which has been at long-term near-zero rates, starts tightening. As the interest-rate differential narrows, carry-trade capital has to find somewhere else to stay.

In one line: the “risk-free yield” of the US dollar is no longer king alone, and global hot money is starting to hesitate about whether to switch cars.

- Medium term: If Japan’s hiking cycle is fully realized, a weaker US dollar index could actually be a forward-looking positive for BTC. Historically, crypto has performed well during weak-dollar periods.

Slightly neutral, leaning toward standing by. 长期唱多黄金的经济学家Peter Schiff在X上发文，称金银正在突破，而比特币在下跌，并且明确说“这不是巧合”。他的逻辑是：五年多来法币购买力持续下滑，一部分投资者本来把BTC当作法币的替代品，现在发现这个“数字法币”本身也在贬值，于是开始寻找别的替代品，黄金成了出口。说白了就是老掉牙的“金比币硬”叙事，但这次赶上BTC实际走弱，杀伤力比平时大一点。BTC现在报$63,469.22，24小时仅微涨0.59%，明显没有强势反驳的底气。

BTC现价63512，24h涨0.72%，高点摸到63564，低点62681。关键点在于：价格已经压过日线R1 63270往上走，还在装「震荡无方向」的，建议先把K线睁开看清楚。

ETH更直接。1902，涨1.17%，24h高1907、低1868，成交额3.01亿USDT，比BNB那0.17亿的存在感强太多。ETH也站上日线R1 1888，短线多头占优不是口号，是价位给的。

资金费率呢？BTC约0.009%，ETH差不多一个数量级，贴着零附近爬。多头在推价格，但杠杆还没开始集体发热。这种结构最容易骗两类人：一类在62681附近止损完，现在又追；一类看见绿了就认定「主升浪」，仓位一次性拉满。

说人话：午间这是修复反弹，不是狂欢派对。量能BTC 3.87亿USDT，撑得起波动，撑不起神话。

方向明确——多头占优。但节奏要冷血：
1. BTC轴心PP 62975是回踩观察位，失守才谈转弱；再下S1 62581是硬支撑区间。
2. 上方先解决63564前高，站不住就别把反弹讲成趋势。
3. ETH守1888续强逻辑在，跌破才降级；1864是防线，丢了就别硬扛叙事。
4. BNB 606附近跟涨无力，R1 607、S1 600，横盘耗时间。
5. XRP在1.00附近磨，R1就是1.00，带不动大盘情绪。

散户最爱把「费率没爆」理解成「还能无限追」。错。费率没爆只说明拥挤度还行，不说明你追在高点就有容错。午间热点就是价格本身：主流币同步站上各自日线R1，空头午盘被动，多头用数据说话。

下一枪看两个结果——BTC能否把63564变成台阶，以及回踩62975时有没有人真接。接得住，偏多延续；接不住，下午就把上午的涨幅吐回去。别找情绪，找价位。

title: 不是所有好消息，都值得消耗一次市场注意力
subTitle:
很多 Web3 项目其实并不缺消息。
产品更新了、主网上线了
增加了一条新链、签了一个合作伙伴
TVL 增长了、交易量上涨了
拿到新的融资、新增了一个重要客户
开发者数量增加了、协议收入创新高

团队内部看起来，每一件事情都很重要。于是最常见的做法是：
发生什么，就发布什么。
但从市场预期管理的角度看，我们通常会先问另一个问题：
这条信息，究竟能够改变市场的什么？
因为市场的注意力是有限的，不是所有真实信息，都值得使用同样的传播资源。更不是所有“利好”，都拥有改变市场预期的能力。

⸻
1. 信息价值 ≠ 市场影响力
这是我们在长期实践中发现的一个很重要的问题。
一条信息对项目内部可能非常重要。但对市场来说，可能几乎没有新增信息。
例如：项目完成了一个持续数月的重要技术升级，对于开发团队来说，这是非常大的里程碑。但普通市场参与者可能完全不知道：这个升级解决了什么问题？为什么以前做不到？升级以后谁会因此改变行为？最终会影响什么？
如果这些问题没有被回答，那么技术价值虽然真实存在，却很难进入市场判断。
所以我们会把两个问题分开：
这件事情本身是否重要？
和：
这件事情是否足以改变市场原来的判断？
这是两件不同的事情。
⸻
2. 我们真正寻找的是“预期差”
市场对任何成熟项目，通常已经存在一个基本判断。
比如：这个项目增长很慢；这个协议没有价值捕获；这个生态只有存量用户；这个产品技术很好，但没有 Adoption；这个项目依赖激励才能维持增长；
这些判断共同构成了市场当前的：
Expectation Baseline｜预期基线。
那么一条信息真正具有市场价值的地方，不是它听起来有多“大”。而是：
它是否提供了足够的新证据，让市场重新审视原来的判断。
真正强的信号，往往来自：
现实与原有预期之间出现了差异。
⸻
3. 所以，我们不会简单地把消息分成“大利好”和“小利好”
Market Expectation Systems 更关注几个维度。
第一：Novelty｜新颖度
市场是否已经知道？如果一件事情已经被充分预期，那么即使最终正式发生，它产生的新增认知也可能很有限。
第二：Expectation Gap｜预期差
它与市场原来的判断之间，有多大的差异？真正容易改变市场预期的信息，通常都在某种程度上打破了旧有认知。
第三：Relevance｜相关性
这件事情与市场当前最关心的问题有没有关系？
信息可能完全真实，却没有进入当前的决策变量。
第四：Credibility｜可信度
这件事情由谁证明？同一个信息，不同证据等级，市场给予的权重完全不同。
第五：Behavioral Potential｜行为潜力
这是我们尤其关注的一层。这条信息被理解以后：
谁会因此改变行为？
如果一条信息只能产生浏览，却几乎无法改变任何参与者的行为，它的长期价值通常有限。
4. 一条强信号，不一定需要很大的传播量
这是一个很容易被忽略的问题。很多项目认为：消息越重要，就应该找越多 KOL 同时发布。
但并不一定。如果信息本身拥有很强的预期差和可信证据，最重要的第一步可能不是“放大”。而是：
建立正确解释。
因为市场第一次如何理解一个新信号，会影响之后整个传播路径。
信号识别必须发生在传播之前。
5. 有些消息应该被放大，有些应该被积累
不是每一个进展都应该独立成为一次 Campaign。
有些信息本身不足以改变市场判断。但如果连续积累三个月，它可能突然变得非常重要。
市场会认为：这不是一次事件，这是趋势。
因此，我们不仅判断：什么值得现在说。还会判断：什么应该暂时积累；什么需要等待验证；什么需要与下一条信号组合；什么应该成为下一轮市场预期更新的核心证据。
6. 真正稀缺的不是消息，而是市场注意力
这是我们非常强调的一点。市场每天需要处理的信息太多了，一个项目不可能要求市场持续关注自己的每一次更新。如果不断使用低强度消息消耗注意力，市场反而会逐渐形成：“这个项目一直在发布消息，但没有真正发生变化。”这会降低未来真正重要信号出现时的敏感度。
所以市场预期管理，本质上也包含：
Attention Allocation｜注意力配置。
什么时候应该保持安静？
什么时候应该开始预热？
什么时候应该集中解释？
什么时候应该让第三方验证？
什么时候应该扩大讨论？
什么时候应该推动行动？
这些选择本身，就是策略的一部分。
7. 这也是 Market Expectation Systems 与普通内容服务的区别
普通内容服务首先问：“这个月需要发多少内容？”
我们首先问：“未来90天，哪些事实可能真正改变市场判断？”
普通 KOL 投放首先问：“需要多少个 KOL？”
我们首先问：
“这条信号现在处于预期形成的哪个阶段，需要什么类型的人完成什么功能？”
普通传播关注：曝光、浏览、点赞、转发。
我们当然也观察这些数据，但我们会继续往后看：市场有没有形成新的解释？讨论内容有没有改变？用户有没有开始主动搜索？社区问题有没有发生变化？产品行为有没有变化？链上行为有没有变化？有没有新的开发者、用户、合作伙伴或者资本开始进入？
因为最终我们需要回答的是：
这条信号，究竟有没有改变市场行为？
8. 我们正在把这种经验变成一套系统
过去很多判断依赖经验。
什么信息重要？
什么时候发布？
先找谁？
市场可能怎样反应？
下一步应该接什么？
这些问题，过去往往存在于少数长期从业者的经验里。
现在，我们正在把这些经验进一步结构化。我们希望逐渐形成一套：
Signal Scoring System｜市场信号评分系统。
它不是简单预测价格。
而是帮助项目判断不同信息可能拥有的：
Attention Impact｜注意力影响
Expectation Impact｜预期影响
Credibility Strength｜证据强度
Behavioral Potential｜行为潜力
Timing Sensitivity｜时间敏感度
最终帮助项目回答一个非常现实的问题：
我们手里的这么多信息，究竟应该把有限的市场资源投入在哪里？
9. 对 Web3 项目方来说，这可能比“更多传播”更重要
Market Expectation Systems 真正希望帮助项目建立的，不是：
“制造更多消息”的能力。
而是：

识别有效信号 → 设计解释 → 形成预期 → 推动行动 → 获取反馈 → 识别下一轮信号。

所以，我们并不认为市场预期管理意味着不断制造声音。恰恰相反，成熟的市场预期管理首先应该知道：
什么时候值得说
说什么
由谁说
什么时候让市场自己开始说。
因为真正强的市场信号，不是声音最大的信息。
而是：
足以让市场重新思考未来的信息。
————
Market Expectation Systems
市场预期管理系统

translatedData.title: Not all good news is worth spending a round of market attention
translatedData.subTitle:
Many Web3 projects actually don’t lack for news.
The product was updated, and the mainnet launched
Added a new chain and signed a partner
TVL is up, and trading volume is up
Received new funding and added an important customer
The number of developers increased, and protocol revenue hit a new high

Inside the team, it looks like every single thing is important. So the most common approach is:
Whatever happens, publish it.
But from the perspective of managing market expectations, we usually ask another question first:
What exactly can this information change in the market?
Because market attention is limited, not all real information is worth using the same amount of promotional resources. And not all “good news” has the ability to change market expectations.

Couldn’t sleep in the middle of the night, and since @Dusk_Foundation  had already been live for months, I got a bit itchy and went ahead to hack together a simple ERC-20 test. The Remix connection was smooth as butter—no bugs at all. But when I checked the on-chain data, I was totally dumbfounded: the contract deployed on DuskEVM’s “skin” was basically exposed—where’s this “native confidentiality”? Turns out the EVM layer isn’t anonymous at all. If you want to hide transaction details, you have to dig into the underlying ZK modules.

I spent the whole night tearing through official docs for a couple of hours, and finally figured out this stitched-together logic:

Base Layer (DuskDS): This is the real accounting backbone. Inside it runs the Moonlight and Phoenix mechanisms—the actual core of anonymity.

Upper Layer Mask (DuskEVM): Essentially an OP Stack–based execution engine. It’s built for Ethereum compatibility, but all data is fully public.

So, if you want to obscure transfer amounts and addresses, users need to switch to Phoenix for the shielding process. Developers have to act as the foreman—tying transparent business logic to the underlying “dark web” settlement. I followed the tutorial end to end, and the cross-domain call gas fees immediately tripled. On top of that, the official examples were written in a patchwork way—one thing after another, none of it in a clean, consistent flow—and my scalp was basically numb with frustration.

Thankfully, the April update didn’t fall apart. Dusk Connect and the new plugin wallet are at least usable—one-click switching between networks, instant switching between clear and dark modes. Finally, I don’t have to manually craft private keys like I did during the early days. Still, from the perspective of an RWA developer, the current underlying environment is at best “workable,” not “smooth enough for production.” This kind of official compromise dual-track system has a cost: it burns through developers’ hair like crazy.

Using DuskEVM to attract old-school Ethereum folks is definitely a good move. But don’t expect the CV method (copy-paste) to solve DeFi privacy. If you really want to understand and capture the benefits of compliant security tokens, you’ll have to bite the bullet and grind through Phoenix’s interaction logic. The development barrier is real, but this RWA chessboard is big—stepping on the learning curve early is absolutely worth it.

China’s July Retail Sales 3.7% Growth Misses Expectations as Industrial Investment Also Slows

Official data released by the National Bureau of Statistics show that in July 2025, growth rates across key indicators—including consumption, industrial output, and fixed-asset investment—generally eased. Total retail sales of consumer goods were clearly below market expectations, becoming the focus of the latest data interpretation. The official assessment is that the national economy is maintaining a generally steady and positive momentum, while also noting that the external environment remains complex and challenging, and that the economy still faces many risks.

On key facts: in July, China’s total retail sales of consumer goods reached CNY 38,780 billion, up 3.7% year over year, slowing by 1.1 percentage points from the previous value and hitting the lowest level for the year. A Caixin survey of domestic and overseas institutions found that economists’ average forecast was 4.8%, with an expected range of 4.1% to 5.5%, meaning the actual reading fell below the lower bound. Retail sales of consumer goods excluding automobiles rose 4.3% year over year, slowing by 0.5 percentage points; after seasonal adjustment, the month-over-month figure fell 0.14%. By consumption type, retail of goods increased 4.0% and catering revenue increased 1.1%. For retailers above designated size, retail sales of goods related to “trade-in for upgrades” in categories such as household appliances and audio-visual equipment, furniture, communication equipment, and cultural/office supplies grew 28.7%, 20.6%, 14.9%, and 13.8%, respectively—still in double digits, but with growth gradually tapering compared with earlier periods. Automobile-related consumption turned negative again, and policy support for autos has clearly weakened. For January–July, retail sales grew 4.8% year over year. The share of online retail sales of physical goods was 24.9%.

In industrial production: in July, the value added of industrial enterprises above designated size increased 5.7% year over year and 0.38% month over month, with the growth rate falling to the lowest in the year. Equipment manufacturing and high-technology manufacturing grew 8.4% and 9.3%, respectively—both faster than the overall pace. Output of 3D printing equipment, industrial robots, and new-energy vehicles rose 24.2%, 24.0%, and 17.1% year over year, respectively. For January–July, the value added of industrial enterprises above designated size increased 6.3% year over year. On investment: for January–July, fixed-asset investment in China (excluding rural households) grew 1.6% year over year; after excluding real estate development investment, it grew 5.3%. By sector, infrastructure investment rose 3.2%, manufacturing investment rose 6.2%, and real estate development investment fell 12.0%. Sales area of newly built commercial housing declined 4.0%, and sales value fell 6.5%. Private investment decreased 1.5% year over year, but increased 3.9% after excluding real-estate developers. In July, fixed-asset investment fell 0.63% month over month. The services production index grew 5.8% year over year in July. Modern services such as information transmission/software and information technology services, and the financial sector, showed stronger momentum.

In terms of logic: the consumption slowdown is linked to the diminishing marginal effects of trade-in for upgrades, the retreat in automobile demand, and continued weakness in contact-intensive consumption such as catering. Industrial production still grew, but momentum has narrowed somewhat; structurally, high-end manufacturing remains relatively stronger. Investment continues to be held back by the real-estate drag, while manufacturing and infrastructure provide the main support. On prices: in July, CPI was flat year over year, while core CPI rose 0.8%. PPI fell 3.6% year over year, and the industrial sector still faces some deflationary pressure. On employment: in July, the national urban surveyed unemployment rate was 5.2%, unchanged from the same month last year. These facts indicate that resilience on the supply side remains, but the recovery on the demand side is uneven.

Impact pathways on the crypto market: this is more of an indirect, lagged, multi-factor observation framework rather than an immediate one-to-one mapping. China’s macro data may affect liquidity conditions and the risk-asset pricing sentiment through global risk appetite, sentiment toward RMB assets and commodities, and market expectations for the strength of steady-growth policies. If the interpretation leans toward slower recovery in domestic demand and an increased need for policy support, some capital may reassess the timing of risk exposure. Conversely, if subsequent policies take effect and improve expectations, it will help stabilize risk appetite. It is important to distinguish that: the above is only a整理 of transmission logic—there is no stable linear relationship between macro readings and the prices of digital assets, which are also jointly constrained by USD liquidity, cross-border capital flows, and international events.

Editor’s view and focus: the information content of this release lies in the fact that the demand-recovery slope remains somewhat slow; policy effects in localized areas such as automobiles are showing a pullback, while high-technology manufacturing and equipment-upgrade related fields are maintaining relatively strong resilience. Going forward, key areas to track include whether existing policy measures are actually landing and whether incremental tools are being strengthened; whether real estate sales and investment can further stabilize; and whether employment and residents’ income can support consumption capacity. For participants in the crypto market, it is more suitable to treat this type of macro information as a medium- to long-term environment variable within a framework, maintain a rational distinction between facts and expectations, and avoid extrapolating a single month’s data directly into short-term market conclusions.

content:
中国7月社零增3.7%不及预期 工业投资同步放缓

国家统计局公布的2025年7月份国民经济运行数据显示，当月消费、工业生产与固定资产投资等主要指标增速整体放缓，其中社会消费品零售总额明显低于市场预期，成为本轮数据解读的焦点。官方总体判断为国民经济保持稳中有进发展态势，同时亦指出外部环境复杂严峻，经济运行仍面临不少风险挑战。

核心事实方面，7月社会消费品零售总额38780亿元，同比增长3.7%，增速较前值放缓1.1个百分点，为年内最低。财新传媒对国内外机构的调查显示，受访经济学家预测均值为4.8%，预测区间为4.1%至5.5%，实际读数低于预期下限。汽车以外的消费品零售额同比增长4.3%，增速放慢0.5个百分点；季调后环比下降0.14%。按消费类型分，商品零售增长4.0%，餐饮收入增长1.1%。限额以上单位中，家用电器和音像器材类、家具类、通讯器材类、文化办公用品类等以旧换新相关商品零售额分别增长28.7%、20.6%、14.9%、13.8%，仍维持两位数，但增速较前期逐渐回落；汽车类消费再度转负，政策对汽车的提振作用明显退坡。1-7月社零同比增长4.8%，实物商品网上零售额占比为24.9%。

工业生产方面，7月全国规模以上工业增加值同比增长5.7%，环比增长0.38%，增速降至年内最低。装备制造业、高技术制造业分别增长8.4%、9.3%，快于整体；3D打印设备、工业机器人、新能源汽车产量同比分别增长24.2%、24.0%、17.1%。1-7月规模以上工业增加值同比增长6.3%。投资方面，1-7月全国固定资产投资（不含农户）同比增长1.6%，扣除房地产开发投资后增长5.3%。分领域看，基础设施投资增长3.2%，制造业投资增长6.2%，房地产开发投资下降12.0%；新建商品房销售面积下降4.0%，销售额下降6.5%。民间投资同比下降1.5%，扣除房开后增长3.9%。7月固定资产投资环比下降0.63%。服务业生产指数7月同比增长5.8%，信息传输软件和信息技术服务业、金融业等现代服务业增势较好。

逻辑拆解上，消费放缓与以旧换新边际效应减弱、汽车需求回落、餐饮等接触型消费仍处低位等因素相关；工业保持增长但动能有所收敛，结构上高端制造相对更强；投资则继续受房地产拖累，制造业与基建形成主要支撑。价格方面，7月CPI同比持平，核心CPI上涨0.8%；PPI同比下降3.6%，工业领域仍面临一定通缩压力。就业上，7月全国城镇调查失业率为5.2%，与上年同月持平。上述事实表明，供给端韧性仍在，需求侧修复并不均衡。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多属于间接、滞后且多因素叠加的观察框架，而非即时映射。中国宏观数据可能通过全球风险偏好、人民币资产与大宗商品情绪、以及市场对稳增长政策力度的预期，影响流动性环境和风险资产定价氛围。若解读偏向内需修复偏慢、政策加力必要性上升，部分资金或重新评估风险敞口节奏；若后续政策显效并改善预期，则有助于稳定风险偏好。需要明确区分的是：上述仅为传导逻辑梳理，宏观读数与数字资产价格之间不存在稳定线性关系，还受到美元流动性、跨境资本流动和国际事件等共同制约。

编辑判断与观察：本次数据的信息量在于，需求修复斜率仍偏缓，政策效果在汽车等局部领域出现退坡，而高技术制造、设备更新相关领域保持相对韧性。后续应重点跟踪存量政策落地与增量工具是否加力、房地产销售和投资能否进一步稳住、以及就业与居民收入对消费能力的支撑。对加密市场参与者而言，更适宜把此类宏观信息作为中长期环境变量纳入框架，保持对事实与预期差的理性区分，避免把单月数据直接外推为短期行情结论。

Slightly bullish but neutral overall. This kind of news won’t show up in tomorrow’s candlestick chart. BTC at $63,394 will likely keep ranging. 🔹 smart contract flexibility in Ethereum
🔹 STARKs for compression and proving operations
🔹 lighter nodes with more decentralization

The Ethereum Foundation Protocol DevOps team officially launched the early testing network for the Glamsterdam upgrade, Platåberget, opening participation to the community.

Unlike the short-term devnet, Platåberget is expected to run for several months, providing a more stable testing environment. The Glamsterdam fork will be activated on this testnet on August 20, and one-click addition of network configuration and the faucet are already available.

Regarding the upgrade roadmap, after incorporating community feedback and implementing it in the clients, the team plans to release a non-final devnet within one month, dedicated to testing abnormal consensus scenarios. After that, the team will proceed with forking long-running testnets such as Sepolia and Hoodi, ultimately rolling out the upgrade to the mainnet.

The core changes of this Glamsterdam upgrade are worth paying close attention to:

Embedded proposer-builder separation (ePBS), writing the PBS mechanism into the protocol layer and reducing reliance on external trust assumptions such as relays.

Block-Level Access Lists, improving Gas experience for cross-contract execution.

A re-pricing of Gas fees, with a lower bound target of about 200 million Gas, increasing L1 throughput.

Increased maximum sizes for contracts and initcode: raising the limits from 24KiB and 48KiB to 64KiB and 128KiB respectively, freeing up space for deploying larger contracts.

It is especially important to note that any tools with hard-coded maximum Gas limits—such as wallets, indexers, and Gas estimators—will be affected. Developers and infrastructure providers need to adapt as soon as possible.

Testnet links and detailed documentation can be found on the Ethereum Foundation blog.#ETH #以太坊 #Glamsterdam

content:
以太坊基金会 Protocol DevOps 团队正式上线 Glamsterdam 升级早期测试网 Platåberget，面向社区开放参与。

与短期 devnet 不同的是，Platåberget 预计持续运行数月，提供更稳定的测试环境。Glamsterdam 分叉将于 8 月 20 日在该测试网上激活，一键添加网络配置与水龙头均已开放。

升级路线图方面，团队在吸收社区反馈、纳入客户端后，计划一个月内推出非最终性 devnet，专门用于测试异常共识场景；之后再推进 Sepolia、Hoodi 等长期测试网的分叉，最终落地主网升级。

本次 Glamsterdam 的核心变化值得重点关注：

内嵌提议者-构建者分离（ePBS），将 PBS 机制写入协议层，减少对中继等外部信任假设。

区块级访问列表（Block-Level Access Lists），改善跨合约执行的 Gas 体验。

Gas 费用重新定价，下限目标约 2 亿 Gas，提升 L1 吞吐。

合约及 initcode 最大体积上限提升，分别由 24KiB、48KiB 提升至 64KiB、128KiB，释放大合约部署空间。

需要特别注意的是，任何硬编码最大 Gas 限制的钱包、索引器、Gas 估算器等工具都将受到影响，开发者与基础设施提供方需要尽快适配。

测试网链接与详细文档可在以太坊基金会博客查看。#ETH #以太坊 #Glamsterdam

Boltz has stopped service, and Blockstream steps in: Bitcoin cross-layer swaps have a new player this time

Blockstream has launched Swaps, connecting the BTC main chain, the Lightning Network, and Liquid, filling the gap left by Boltz’s pause.

If you’ve played with the Lightning Network, you know Boltz well—it’s the most commonly used atomic swap service between on-chain BTC and the Lightning Network. It paused service recently, which is like a main highway for cross-layer transfers suddenly being blocked. What Blockstream is launching this time—Blockstream Swaps—allows the BTC main chain, Lightning, and Liquid to be swapped between each other. This is a plug-in at the infrastructure layer. In simple terms: the road is fixed with a new one—and it’s being repaired by Blockstream, an established infrastructure company.

In one sentence: it’s not new money entering the market—it’s old players rebuilding the broken bridge.

Impact on the market
- Short term: purely an infrastructure update, with no added capital involved, so it barely moves prices. BTC is currently around $63,394.37, with only a 0.51% 24h fluctuation, suggesting the market isn’t treating this as a tradable narrative.
- Medium term: improved ecosystem resilience. Boltz’s shutdown exposed the Lightning Network’s reliance on a single service provider. Now that there’s a fallback option, Layer2 infrastructure is becoming less centralized and less dependent on one point. This is good for long-term network security, but price transmission is likely to be slow.

My take
Neutral—wait and watch. BTC has been stuck around $63,394 in a range-bound pattern. This kind of infrastructure news won’t change the trend direction; what truly determines short-term moves is macro liquidity. ETH is at $1,896.27 as well and hasn’t been affected by this news. To see this news become a price catalyst, we’d need to wait for actual transaction volume data for Swaps. The risk is that the new service just launched and hasn’t yet gone through a large-scale pressure test—don’t jump to conclusions.

In the afternoon I stared at the order book of $PLUME  and suddenly thought of one of Livermore’s sayings.

He said most people lose money—not because they make the wrong call, but because they’re unwilling to admit they’re wrong.

That chance to admit it is disappearing second by second.

0.012600 is down, but not aggressively; in 24 hours it’s only 1.56%. Yet the $82 million USDT in trading is smashed into it—like a dull knife slowly grinding flesh.

I’m too familiar with this kind of chart.

In my head I kept saying, I’ll wait a bit more—what if it rebounds? My fingers just wouldn’t press the stop-loss button. Only after it really breaks down do I comfort myself by saying, “I’ll hold for the long term.”

But there’s no “long term” at all—just that I can’t face the fact that I chased after the price higher.

Livermore put it very bluntly. I don’t remember his exact wording, but the meaning is—go ahead and fool anyone, but don’t fool your own account.

Next time, I have to let go before I run out of breath.

#BTC #ETH #PLUME #投资哲学 #Trading Mindset

content:
下午盯着 $PLUME 的盘口，忽然想到利弗莫尔那句话。

利弗莫尔说得很直白，原话忘了，意思就是——你骗谁都行，别骗自己的账户。

我下次得在没断气前先松手。

Second, look for a “can’t drop any further” kind of signal—volume shrinking while the price drifts down, and then it’s gradually pulled back after falling. It may not be a full reversal, but at least it suggests panic is easing.

My rhythm is simple: don’t chase highs, don’t go all-in. The position in my hands is always one that lets me sleep. For mainstream coins like BTC and ETH, what you’re really trading is patience. A week ago, ETH was still grinding for a bottom around $ 1850, but today it’s back to $ 1899—up 1% over the past 24 hours. On the surface, not much, right? But compare it to a month ago—back then ETH had already fallen to a level that made people doubt reality.

The market sentiment index is 31, and the whole market reeks of fear. I’m way too familiar with this kind of atmosphere. In March 2020, June 2022, and that wave last year—every time the market is in extreme fear, someone always asks me, "How much lower can it go? Should we run?"

But I want to ask you something instead: **when everyone is afraid, what is actually happening?**

ETH is down 62% from its all-time high—do you understand what that number means? It means most people have already completely exited. The remaining ones are either deep believers or the numb-and-holding crowd. Neither group will dump and sell heavily at this moment.

Meanwhile, over on Wall Street, people are still obsessing over private chains, thinking their so-called "closed gardens" are safer. I agree with that.

The real value of blockchain lies in openness. Private chains may seem "controllable" in the short term, but five years from now, ten years from now—what then? Technical standards follow the ecosystem. Whose ecosystem is bigger and whose users are more, that party defines the rules. ETH is still the most complete smart-contract platform among public chains, and that foundation hasn’t changed.

**So what does this translate to in practice?**

I’ll state my judgment directly: this round of ETH stabilizing around $ 1830 isn’t fundamentally a technical signal—it’s a sentiment signal. When the market is terrified to the extreme, that’s when selling pressure is typically the lightest. Recently when I was watching Dusk, I actually didn’t pay much attention to TPS. My focus stayed on one question: “When does a transaction truly count as finished?” 

In the past, when I saw confirmation speed, I usually just looked at whether the numbers were fast. Later, I encountered a cross-chain wait once: the page showed success, but I still didn’t dare to immediately take the next step, because I didn’t know whether that status would change again. During those few minutes, whether it was fast or slow stopped mattering—I just wanted a clear answer.#ETH  

Dusk’s Succinct Attestation provides a deterministic finality. After the block goes through proposal, validation, and confirmation, the state can be settled, without needing to keep waiting through many more rounds to feel at ease. The official documentation puts the finality time at about 10 seconds.

In simple transfers, this might not feel very exciting, but it becomes very practical in scenarios like securities, or synchronized settlement between assets and payments. The money has already been paid—whether there is final confirmation on the assets side can’t be left to both parties refreshing their pages and guessing.#BTC  

What I understand now about Dusk is that it’s really about solving this kind of waiting where you “don’t dare to proceed to the next step.” Ten seconds isn’t a number to shout as a slogan; the key is whether, after those 10 seconds, participants can be confident to continue operating. As for whether it remains stable during real peak times, I’ll keep monitoring the network’s actual performance.#dusk  $DUSK  @Dusk_Foundation

GENIUS Act officially takes effect: the first federal rules for stablecoins—this time it’s not crackdowns, it’s licensing

The U.S. has set up a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, removing the biggest compliance hurdle that kept institutional capital from entering.

With the GENIUS Act officially becoming law, this is the first comprehensive federal stablecoin regulatory framework in U.S. history. In plain terms: issuing stablecoins used to be a gray area, and when institutions wanted to make large-scale allocations to U.S. dollar stablecoins, their legal departments were the first to object. Now there are clear requirements for reserves, audits, and licensing. Circle, issuers, and custodians all have rules to follow. One-sentence translation: stablecoins have moved from “underground money shops” to “licensed banks,” and Wall Street’s money can enter with legitimacy.

💡 Positive. This is one of the most valuable regulatory tailwinds in this cycle.

Market impact
- Short term: Compliance expectations heat up. Funds flow toward stablecoin issuers and related targets. Around BTC $63,524.21, sentiment is relatively warm. ETH $1,897.69, as the main settlement network for stablecoins, benefits directly from expectations of increased issuance. But note: BTC is up only 0.80% over 24 hours, meaning the news has been partially digested already—it’s not an uncut, pure bullish catalyst.
- Medium term: Global regulation is shifting from confrontation to formal rulemaking. Europe’s MiCA, as well as Hong Kong and Singapore, will likely follow suit through competitive regulation. Each step up in stablecoin issuance expands on-chain settlement demand in parallel, strengthening ETH’s long-term logic.

Clearly bullish, but don’t chase. Regulatory tailwinds are a slow-moving variable; price action is more likely to consolidate and trend upward rather than surge in a straight line. #dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Encryption circles have a deeply rooted obsession: “Only recognize private keys, not people.” For ordinary cryptocurrencies, losing the key means permanently destroying the funds. But if you impose these rules on on-chain stocks or bonds, the whole thing becomes absurd. Imagine the user’s hardware cold wallet is damaged, or a court has already issued a clear ruling on the ownership of an asset—do these real, hard-earned, legally owned properties really have to be locked away forever together with that abandoned address?

Recently, while carefully studying Dusk ($DUSK)’s technical documentation on regulated assets, I found an interesting detail: the official elevates an “asset recovery and error-correction” mechanism to a level comparable to that of transfer transactions and compliant audits. In reality, no financial system can stay perfectly calm forever—it must face extreme scenarios such as lost cryptographic credentials, hacker theft, and judicial intervention.

However, “allowing recovery” is a double-edged sword. If the project team can simply provide a super-administrator account that can transfer funds at will, then what people hold no longer constitutes true ownership—it’s merely a string of code in someone else’s database that can be tampered with at any time.

A compliant and restrained remediation process must absolutely not be a simple, brute-force “one-click override.” It has to answer several hard questions: Who is allowed to submit a recovery request? What level of real-world evidence must be produced to be considered valid? Is a mandatory public notice and waiting period required? At what point is the old address fully frozen? Can all operational traces be made publicly available for the entire network to review and verify?

In this regard, Dusk’s approach is very restrained. It doesn’t apply a rigid, one-size-fits-all recovery template to all securities. Instead, it only provides identity verification, underlying smart contracts, and settlement primitives. As for the specific rule standards, the issuing institution can flexibly tailor them according to the particular laws of its country.

Total inability to recover means real-world legitimate rights can be erased completely by a single mistake. Meanwhile, a recovery right without supervision would turn decentralization into mere empty talk. Whether you can lock down both ends at once—protecting private property as sacred and inviolable, while also preventing privilege from doing harm—is the real litmus test for the quality of RWA and on-chain securities infrastructure.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Those who understand the rule of “buying coins” know this: whoever holds the mnemonic phrase holds the money. If you lose the key, you can only accept your fate. This kind of gameplay is fine when you’re talking about native crypto assets, but if we’re discussing tokenized equity or real-world bonds, things are completely different. Suppose an investor’s hardware wallet fails, a custodian has an issue, or a court has already issued a property judgment—should these legitimate assets really be “buried along with” the old address?

When I was recently reviewing Dusk ($DUSK)’s regulatory asset-architecture documentation, I found that they place “remediation and recovery” mechanisms at a very core position—on par with everyday transfers and audits. In plain terms, real financial operations can’t be nothing but smooth, easy transactions; they must have the ability to handle messy situations like credential loss, fraud, and legal enforcement.

But there’s a fatal contradiction here: “recovery mechanisms” are very easy to be turned into tools for wrongdoing. If the issuing entity holds some kind of “God-mode” permission that can freely debit funds, then what exactly are retail buyers buying ownership of? It’s not ownership at all—just an internal balance that can be modified at any time. Therefore, a reliable recovery process must stand up to scrutiny: Who is eligible to initiate it? What evidence counts as valid? Do we need a public notice period in the middle to prevent fraud? When is the original address locked permanently? Can the entire operation withstand public verification?

One thing that’s fairly straightforward about Dusk is that it doesn’t directly force the market to adopt a rigid, generic template. What it provides are the underlying “building blocks” of identity verification, smart contracts, and settlement. As for how the specific rules are set, the issuer assembles them according to the laws in its jurisdiction.

At the end of the day, the core difficulty of on-chain securitization is getting the boundaries right. Completely locking everything down ignores real, legitimate rights; but if recovery is allowed without limits, it degenerates into a centralized server. Balancing both ends at once—without backdoors and without creating dead records—is the true test of a project’s competence.

三个周期我读成「日线修复还在、4h 卡在均线带里、1h 刚从超卖弹起来」。1h：价格 1898 已经爬回 MA7（约 1889）和 MA25（约 1883）上方，MA50 还在头顶压着，RSI14 从早盘的超卖区弹到 50 中性附近，MACD 柱翻红但 DIF 还在零轴下方——小时级是超跌反抽，不是主升，别追。4h：价格被 MA7/MA25/MA50 三道裹在中间，MA99 在脚下托，RSI14 回到 45 偏弱区，MACD 柱刚有收窄迹象，属于跌破后在中部磨的弱势整理，1900 整数口 + 4h 均线黏合带是第一道坎。日线最关键：MA7 压头、MA25 在脚托，RSI14 还有 52 中性，MACD 红柱但缩口——从 7 月底那轮从 1700 拉起来的修复结构没破，只是 1950 上方连续两周回不去，日线大结构在 1870-1950 这个箱子里慢慢磨。

关键位划死：上方 1911.66 日内高 + 1900 整数口是第一道坎，今晚摸了 1911 没站住，过不去就是弱；再上 1950 是这轮短线命门，也是 4h MA50/日 MA7 重合带，拿下才谈重新站回平台。下方 1868 日内低 + 日 MA25 支撑叠区，回踩不破才认横盘有效；真跌破 1850，节奏就松了，1800 整数口是中线最后一道软防线。

💧 衍生品与情绪
永续资金费率 0.00006141（8h，约日化 +0.0184%），微正不热，多头没上头、空头也没逼空，双方都冷静。未平仓 2,383,104 ETH（约 45.25 亿 USDT 名义），持仓不低，说明这波反弹是真有仓位在守。但多空账户比全球多头占 70.5%、多空比 2.39，顶尖交易员多空比 1.38——账面一边倒看多，价格却只是弱反弹，这种「人看多、价不涨」的局最容易被插针扫多。ETH/BTC 0.02987 仍在近 30 天相对低位区间，资金没明显往 ETH 轮动。Fear&Greed 这块精确实时值我这边拉不到不编，但从费率中性偏正、OI 偏高看，没有大规模爆仓或资金外逃信号，杠杆情绪偏温。

📰 消息面
实时新闻抓取通道当前不可用，抓不到直接拉/砸 ETH 的单一硬催化，不编具体事件。能确认的是衍生品层面没异常（费率中性偏正、OI 偏高但没到极端），宏观上今晚风险情绪偏中性，ETH 这种大市值 alt 在没催化时弹性不如山寨，今晚这波更像是「1868 技术支撑 + 空头回补」驱动，而非单条消息引爆。链上质押率、Gas、ETF 净流入这些精确实时数字公开通道今天也拉不到，不瞎编。

👉 我的看法
短线我把 ETH 读成「1870-1950 箱体 + 超跌反抽 + 等待方向」。今晚实质进展只是 1h 从超卖弹回均线带下沿，但 4h 还裹在均线带里、日线大结构没破也没强，告诉我这波大概率还要在 1870-1950 再晃一阵，别急着认反转。操作上，没仓的别在 1898 盲接，等两件事之一：要么放量站回 1911 且回踩不破，我才认短空缓和；要么回调到 1868-日 MA25 叠区企稳再轻仓上车，胜率比现在高。有仓的把止损挂在 1850 下方，多空比 2.39 偏多、OI 45 亿不低，插针扫单最容易打掉追着情绪进的杠杆。中线只要日线重新站回 1950 且 MACD 柱翻红、ETH/BTC 守 0.03 上方，我才认中期结构翻多、打开往 2100；1868 不破就还是偏强区间，破了就重新打开往 1800 去的空间。仓位控小，这种窄幅局插针振幅比想象中狠。

I’d looked into Fusionist before. It’s a AAA-grade game built with the Unity engine, so the fundamentals are there. But at this current spot—around 0.19—honestly it’s a bit awkward. If I had to participate, I’d prefer waiting for it to hold above 0.18 before entering. Stop-loss at 0.165, upside target 0.23. Don’t ask me why—just that I’ve been trapped too many times by this “overheated short-covering rebound” setup, and I’ve learned.

PORTAL has the largest volume—378M USDT—but the gain is only 36%, which means selling pressure isn’t small either. The narrative of “bring ten billion players into Web3” is good, but the GameFi sector has gotten a bit oversaturated lately, and at a price of 0.0167, liquidity still isn’t quite enough. My advice is to just take a look. Unless it breaks out above 0.02 with strong volume, don’t jump in lightly.

Let’s mention STAR too. It’s up 31%, but funding rate is 0.0844%—longs are overheated. Be careful. Generally, with a data combination like this, there’s likely to be a pullback afterward. If you already hold it, you can consider taking profits in batches. If you don’t have it, don’t chase.

AIO and DIA are also up nicely, but honestly, I can’t really say how sustainable these mid-cap coins are. Market sentiment comes fast and leaves fast too—don’t ask me how I know; it’s all lessons learned.

As for what’s trending on search/HOT: HYPE, PUMP, CASHCAT—those names alone make people itch to jump in. But I urge everyone to stay calm. Especially with animal coins like CASHCAT—how long has it been sitting on the gainers list? Up 10% today, and it could drop 15% tomorrow. Retail investors can’t play these games against well-informed players.

BTC and ETH are still the main base. Focus on positioning and allocation rather than chasing hotspots every day.

Finally, here’s my overall thinking. The Fear & Greed Index is 50 right now—neutral and slightly cold—meaning the market hasn’t reached “crazy” levels yet. That’s actually a good sign. If BTC around 63,500 can hold, there might be a small rebound next week. But don’t expect it to directly break through 65,000—that would require fresh catalysts.

For alts: what’s up hard today will most likely differentiate tomorrow. If you’re quick, you can play short-term trades; if you’re slower, be honest and hold onto the major coins and wait for the wind to come. Remember: in crypto, staying alive matters more than anything—don’t assume you can catch every wave of the market.

Oh, by the way—do you think this GPS move is a one-off spike or the real start of a trend? Drop your thoughts in the comments. I want to see if I’m not the only one who feels awful for missing the move.

Over the past 24 hours, roughly $186 million in liquidations occurred across the entire market, as both longs and shorts were hit again. About $107 million in short positions were liquidated, while about $78.63 million in long positions were liquidated—shorts suffered a significantly larger loss.

Structurally, this wave of liquidations was mainly driven by BTC and ETH: <$BTC > liquidations of approximately $37.6174 million, and <$ETH > liquidations of approximately $35.1261 million; together, they already account for more than 39% of the total liquidations across the market. The sharp fluctuations in major assets are the core reason this round of liquidations was amplified.

Normally, when the liquidation amount for shorts is significantly higher than for longs, it often indicates a quick rebound in price—funds that went short against the trend get concentratedly cleared. Conversely, if longs account for a larger share of liquidations, it typically corresponds to a rapid sell-off. This time, the shorts were essentially “blood-washed,” suggesting that the strength of the short-term rebound is not weak.

However, it’s important to note that $186 million is not extreme when viewed against the overall size of the entire crypto market. Liquidation data is more like a “thermometer” for sentiment and leverage—it can reflect a temporary imbalance between longs and shorts, but it does not necessarily predict a trend reversal. What truly determines direction remains macro liquidity, ETF fund flows, and changes in on-chain fundamentals.

For ordinary traders, the biggest thing to watch in this kind of market is not direction, but leverage. On high-volatility assets like BTC and ETH, going heavy with high leverage can easily force you out in a single sharp wick. The market’s “win” has nothing to do with you, but the volatility is bought by you.

For short-term trading, it’s recommended to monitor whether liquidation is accompanied by a surge in trading volume and a decline in open interest. This often means leverage has been effectively flushed out, making the subsequent move more sustainable. If, on the other hand, volume quickly dries up after the liquidations, be alert to the risk of a second deeper test.

Today I reopened the Dusk website. Before looking at the promotional copy, I noted the product status one by one.
Dusk’s native L1 is marked as Live; Dusk Trade is marked as Building; both DuskEVM and Hedger are still on Testnet.
These terms are more useful than “RWA,” “institutional-grade,” or “compliant finance,” because they separate what’s already running from what’s still being built.#ETH 
At the moment, what’s truly live is the underlying network. The data shown on the website says: more than 210 million DUSK are participating in staking, with a deterministic finality/settlement time of about 10 seconds. At least here, you can observe that the network security and settlement layer already exist, rather than it being only a thing mentioned in a whitepaper.
Dusk Trade is still in Building. The official documentation describes it as an application layer for tokenized financial assets. In the future, it should connect asset discovery, investor onboarding/eligibility, wallet binding, trading operations, payment coordination, and settlement. In other words, it’s not just a regular DEX with an RWA label—it’s an attempt to put the whole process surrounding a regulated asset trade into a single entry point.
But if it’s “under construction,” it should be evaluated as such. For now, I won’t count planned stocks, bonds, or money-market funds as chain transaction volume that has already been generated.#BTC 
The website also lists an issuance confirmation size of over 300 million euros, as well as more than 50,000 potential investors covering crypto users and partner organizations. To me, the significance of these two numbers isn’t to prove success—it’s to set benchmarks for later verification: when will these confirmed assets truly enter Dusk Trade? How many potential investors will complete wallet binding and eligibility checks? And ultimately, how much sustained trading volume will remain?
This is also the most critical part of the $DUSK  value pathway. The underlying layer can already support staking and settlement, but to keep Gas and application activity growing, we still need Dusk Trade, DuskEVM, and the privacy components to move from Building/Testnet into real usage.
I’d rather accept a progress schedule that isn’t perfectly tidy. Writing out Live, Building, and Testnet clearly is far more trustworthy than packaging all future plans as “already delivered.”

#termmax @termmax  If the borrowing cost of funds could be attached directly to buy and sell orders—just like trading crypto assets—would decentralized lending still remain pure in nature? This is the biggest thought TermMax has brought to me.

After reading the 2026 TMX whitepaper and taking a deep dive into its core architecture, I found that it has long stepped beyond the simple “fixed income” framework. Its essence lies in a thorough “dissection” of the lending contracts that were originally glued together. Within its system, FT acts as a zero-coupon instrument for maturity settlement; meanwhile, borrowers effectively lock in their financing costs upfront by offloading the related XT tranche. The truly disruptive aspect is that interest on funds is no longer merely an add-on after a borrowing action is completed—it is brought forward and becomes an independent asset that both sides can publicly quote for before any trade occurs.

The full rollout of TermMax V2 pushes this logic to the extreme. With Limit Orders covering the entire set of business lines, lenders can define their desired minimum returns, while borrowers can draw the red line of how much cost they can tolerate. Then, the Order Aggregator filters and assembles orders across massive instruction sets. This is not only an upgrade in user experience—it also signals that a “rate-matching platform” with some scale is starting to take shape. The market no longer relies on a single algorithmic curve; instead, it is driven by real bilateral quotes, willingness to take the other side, and optimal path searching.

However, the other side of the coin is the liquidity trap that is amplified as a result. Locking in a rate does not eliminate pricing risk. If the price range of the placed orders becomes disconnected from the actual supply and demand for funds, the so-called “system-optimal solution” is very likely to be an incorrect valuation compromised due to insufficient liquidity depth. Under the matching mechanism, a shortage of market-making funds can force ordinary participants to bear extremely high implicit slippage.

So, I’m inclined to stay cautious and not crown TermMax as an “on-chain interest rate exchange” for now. The key points to watch next are whether borrowing periods that vary in length can truly crystallize into a smooth yield curve—and whether those limit orders can trigger genuine buy-sell interactions in a meaningful sense. The answers to these questions will decide whether it can secure a key position in the industry.#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  如果资金的借用成本能够像交易加密资产那样，直接挂上买卖单等待撮合，去中心化借贷的性质还纯粹吗？这是 TermMax 给我带来的最大思考。

阅读了 2026 年的 TMX 白皮书，并深入拆解其核心架构后，我发现它早已跳出了“固定收益”的简单框架。其精髓在于将原本粘合在一起的借贷合约，进行了一场彻底的“解剖”。在它的体系内，FT 充当了到期给付的零息票据；而借款方借由脱手相关的 XT 份额，实质上是在前端锁死了自身的融资开销。这种机制的颠覆性在于，资金利息不再是借钱动作完成后的附属品，而是直接前置化，演变为一个可以在交易发生前由市场双方公开喊价的独立标的。

TermMax V2 的全面铺开，更是将这套逻辑推向了极致。随着 Limit Order 覆盖至全部业务线，出借人能圈定保底的收益诉求，借款人亦可画出成本的承受红线。随后，Order Aggregator 负责在海量指令中进行筛选与拼凑。这不仅是用户体验的升级，更标志着一个初具规模的“利率撮合平台”正在成型。市场不再依赖单一的算法曲线，而是由真实的双边报价、接盘意愿以及最优路径搜索来驱动。

然而，硬币的另一面是随之放大的流动性陷阱。锁定利率绝不等于消灭了定价风险。倘若挂单的价格区间与实际的资金供需出现断层，所谓的“系统最优解”，大概率只是一个因为缺乏资金深度而妥协的错误估值。在撮合机制下，做市资金的匮乏会让普通的参与者承担极高的隐性滑点。

因此，我倾向于保持谨慎，暂时不给 TermMax 戴上“链上利率交易所”的王冠。接下来的核心看点，在于那些长短不一的借款周期，能否真实沉淀出一根平滑的收益率曲线？那些限价单能否激发真正意义上的买卖交锋？这些问题的答案，才是决定其行业地位的关键。#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  I used to think DeFi lending is just a pool where people park funds to earn interest—then use collateral to borrow money. But after reading the 2026 version of the TMX whitepaper carefully, I realized TermMax plays a much deeper game. If the borrowing interest could be treated just like buying and selling spot—posting orders directly on the order book for others to take—then this market wouldn’t be just simple lending anymore.

When I first came across TermMax, I thought it was merely a tool for locking costs. But after breaking down how its FT and XT work, I understood that the real highlight is “debt fragmentation.” In this system, FT functions as a zero-coupon debt instrument that is repaid at maturity. As long as a borrower sells the corresponding assets they hold, they can lock in future funding costs in advance. This means interest is no longer a blind-box number you passively accept after borrowing—you get the real negotiating chips on the table before the trade.

Look at the V2 version’s fully rolled-out Limit Order (limit price order) functionality as well. It makes this kind of game concrete. If you want to provide funds, you can fill in the minimum yield you’re willing to accept; if you want to borrow, you can set an upper limit on your maximum cost. Then, finally, everything is stitched together by the Order Aggregator. It’s like building a market for trading “access rights to capital,” where some people post prices and others bargain, while the underlying system searches for the most suitable path.

However, when the gameplay changes, new traps appear too. Don’t assume it becomes fixed interest so you can rest easy—there’s still the risk of pricing deviation. If the numbers everyone posts on the board don’t match the actual circulating supply-and-demand for funds, then the so-called “optimal solution” the system matches automatically may simply be a price that happens to result in a trade—at the expense of a poor sucker.

So at this stage, I’m not in a rush to praise it as a revolutionary “interest rate exchange.” I’d rather wait a bit: first, see whether it can produce a solid yield curve across different borrowing tenors; then, see whether the orders people post can truly generate competition; and finally, examine the price spread between it and traditional floating interest to determine whether it offers a rational logic. Those are the key tests of its real quality.#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  以前总觉得 DeFi 借贷也就是个存钱吃息、抵押拿钱的池子。但仔细读完 2026 版 TMX 白皮书后，我发现 TermMax 把这盘棋下得深得多。要是借钱的利息也能像买卖现货一样，直接在盘口挂单等别人来吃，那这个市场可就不止是简单的借贷了。

最早接触 TermMax 时，我以为它单纯只是给咱们提供一个锁死成本的工具。但拆解了它的 FT 和 XT 玩法后，才明白真正的看点在于“债务碎片化”。在这个系统里，FT 扮演着到期还本的零息债角色；借款人只要把手里对应的资产卖出，就能把未来的资金开销提前定死。这就意味着，利息不再是你借完钱后被动承受的盲盒数字，而是你在交易前就能拿到台面上真刀真枪去博弈的筹码。

再看看 V2 版本全面铺开的 Limit Order（限价单）功能，更是把这种博弈做实了。你想放款，可以自己填个能接受的最低收益；你想拿钱，也能设个最高成本的红线，最后靠着 Order Aggregator 去做订单缝合。这就好比搭起了一个炒“资金使用权”的集市，有人喊价、有人砍价，底层系统负责寻找最合适的路径。

不过，玩法一变，新的坑也跟着来了。别以为变成固定利率就能高枕无忧，定价偏离的风险依然存在。一旦盘面上大家挂出来的数字，跟真实流通的资金供需对不上号，系统自动匹配出来的所谓“最优解”，很可能只是一个恰好能成交的冤大头价格罢了。

所以，我现阶段并不会急着吹捧它是革命性的“利率交易所”。我更愿意让子弹飞一会儿：先看看它以后能不能在各种借款期限里，跑出一条扎实的收益率曲线；看看大家挂的单子能不能真的卷出竞争；最后再盯一下它跟传统浮动利息之间的价差，到底能不能给出一个符合常理的逻辑。这些才是检验它成色的关键。#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  Recently, I used Pendle's PT-sUSDe as collateral to take out a 30-day USDC fixed-interest loan on TermMax. Honestly, the product’s frontend interaction is really well done—you can get it done in one click. Compared with manually looping on Aave, it’s definitely less hassle. At first, I watched the borrowing cost locked on the books at 8% and thought I had the cost tightly under control. But only after I repaid the debt and did a full review did I realize that in crypto markets, buying this kind of “certainty” often comes with unexpected costs.

The most painful part of this trade is the extremely high loss if you exit early. The platform’s underlying logic is to package your borrowing instrument as an FT and throw it into the pool for trading. By day 15, I found a new opportunity and wanted to close out and leave. Unfortunately, at that time, market interest rates were falling, which caused the FT price—basically like a zero-coupon bond—to rise along with yields. To get my collateral back, I had to bite the bullet and buy back the FT at the then-higher market price. After going through all that, the actual blended annualized cost ended up around 14%. Sure, holding it to maturity does let you lock in the 8%, but in the on-chain world where one day can outperform a whole year of traditional finance market action, how many active players would truly keep their position “welded” for an entire month with zero movement?

Let’s also talk about the so-called seamless rolling over. Even there, the variables can’t be ignored. Even if the product supports one-click switching into next month’s new pool, your funding costs still depend on the AMM’s mood. On the day I renewed, the interest on the new contract jumped straight from 8% to 11.5%. This kind of blind-box pricing is impossible to predict.

And don’t even get me started on the friction costs from on-chain interactions. Because it involves the generation of the instrument tokens and complex underlying routing, placing an order here uses 40% more Gas than Aave. I only put in 5,000u, and the chain immediately deducted 12 bucks in fees. When you spread that cost over the 30-day cycle, it’s like the fee rate quietly rises by nearly 3% again. For small players who come here to lever up, it’s basically doing charity for the node operators.

In the end, institutions and big players pursue duration matching. Us retail folks want freedom to enter and exit. This TermMax setup is basically profiting from the money you “stick it out to the end.” #eth $ETH

这笔买卖最让人头疼的地方，在于中途离场的极高折损。该平台的底层逻辑，是把你的借款凭证包装成 FT 扔进池子里交易。到了第 15 天我有了新标的，打算结账走人，偏偏那会儿大环境利率在掉，导致这种类似零息债券的 FT 价格水涨船高。为了拿回抵押物，我只能捏着鼻子按当时偏高的市价把 FT 扫回来。这么一折腾，实际付出的综合年化硬是干到了 14% 左右。虽说死扛到期确实能稳拿 8%，但在一天跑完传统金融一年行情的链上世界，有几个活跃玩家会真把仓位焊死整整一个月毫无动作？

再聊聊所谓的无缝滚仓，这里头的变数同样不容忽视。哪怕产品支持一键切入下个月的新池子，但资金成本全看 AMM 的脸色。我点续期的那天，新合约的利息直接从 8% 蹦到了 11.5%。这种开盲盒一样的定价机制，毫无预期可言。

更别提链上交互那要命的摩擦成本了。由于牵涉到凭证代币的生成以及复杂的底层路由，在这里开单的单笔 Gas 消耗要比 Aave 贵出 40% 之多。我这单只放了 5000u 进去，链上直接扣掉 12 刀的手续费。把这笔开销折算进 30 天的周期里，相当于费率又偷偷摸摸涨了将近 3%。小户来这里加杠杆，简直是给节点做慈善。

说到底，机构大户才去追求久期匹配，咱们散户图的就是个进出自由。TermMax 这套固定玩法，其实是在赚你“死拿到底”的钱。#eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  A few days ago, I tried collateralized borrowing on TermMax. I used Pendle’s PT-sUSDe to borrow USDC and set the term to 30 days. The platform focuses on ultra-minimal operations, so compared to Aave it really saves a few steps of tedious interactions. At the time, the UI showed an 8% annualized borrowing rate, which looked quite attractive—but when I actually settled the bill, it suddenly hit me: the so-called “fixed cost” has too much fluff.

The core issue is the hidden penalty for exiting early. The protocol’s setup is to convert the debt into FT and place it in a secondary pool. When my borrowing reached day 15, I wanted to close the position early, but I happened to hit a period when market rates were falling. Since FT is a zero-coupon bond, the closer you are to the settlement date, the more expensive it becomes. At that moment, the market price had already been pushed up very high. I had to bite the bullet and buy back FT at that inflated price to settle the debt. After digging through the statement, the actual annualized rate jumped to around 14%. My group chat friends said if you just hold to the end, you can keep the 8%, but in crypto—where there’s a new hotspot every day—who’s willing to freeze their money for a whole month and do nothing?

Let me also talk about the renewal trap. The one-click roll/extend feature looks thoughtful, but the new pool’s pricing is completely driven by the AMM. On the day I operated, the interest rate for the new cycle shot from 8% to 11.5% with zero certainty.

Fees are another big one. Even though one-click leverage is convenient, the per-transaction Gas cost is about 40% higher than Aave. That’s because it involves FT minting and more complex underlying routing. For my principal of 5000u, just the on-chain transit fees were $12—when you work it out, it effectively bumped up the annualized rate by nearly 3%. For retail users participating with small amounts, it’s basically like paying to give money away.

All in all, traditional finance plays the fixed-duration matching game, while DeFi players want fast in and fast out. TermMax’s mechanism only makes sense if you’re absolutely certain you can hold the PT through to maturity and never cut the position mid-way. The moment you have even a little uncertainty about how you might need to reallocate funds, it’s much more sensible—and definitely cheaper—to go back and use Aave to bear the floating rate. #eth $ETH
